3 photographs attached, in order:
  1. front three-quarter across the square: central clock tower, corner pavilions and steep slate roofs, daylight
  2. three-quarter from a bridge along the river side, showing the long wing, towers and mansard roofs
  3. view along the long flank facade with its repeated arched bays and mansard roof

json.notes: The Hôtel de Ville is a long, heavy Second Empire block of pale stone, about 22 m to the eaves, under a steep grey slate mansard with dormers. Its signature features are a tall central clock belfry with an open lantern and spire, set on the front wing, and steep pavilion roofs on the front corners. I model the main mass, the mansard, two corner pavilions and the belfry tower, with the stone walls, slate roofs and punched windows.
